title: POC scoping: Latency & Throughput SLOs - Igneous Data
summary: AE + SE ran a detailed POC scoping focused on latency and throughput SLOs. Customer wants clear TTFT vs TPOT definitions, p95/p99 targets, and a measurement plan that captures cold vs warm KV cache and production-like concurrency. Action items include Redwood to run a first-pass benchmark, share test harness and config, and schedule a 2-week load test window.
next_steps: Redwood to run baseline benchmark and share results (due 2027-01-25)
Customer to provide 48-hour production traffic trace and sample prompts (due 2027-01-20)
Schedule load-test window and invite stakeholders (tentative 2027-01-28 to 2027-02-11)
Redwood to share security questionnaire and SOC2 summary
action_items: Alex Mercer - Run 3x benchmark profiles: cold KV, warm KV, and steady-state TPOT measurement (due 2027-01-25)
Priya Singh - Prepare load-test harness config and shared script, include 95th/99th percentile reporting and raw latency traces (due 2027-01-22)
Marta Lopez - Share representative 48-hour traffic trace + sample prompts and success criteria doc (due 2027-01-20)
Jon Park - Provide VPC networking constraints and avg concurrency expectations (due 2027-01-21)
Tina Wu - Confirm required encryption/KMS controls and review SOC2 artifacts (due 2027-01-24)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. agenda is to scope the POC around latency and throughput SLOs, specifically definining TTFT vs TPOT and how we'll measure p95/p99. I'm gonna hand to Priya to kick off on approach.

[00:25] Priya (SE): cool, quick intro, we typically split metrics two ways: TTFT — time to first token, that's client-perceivable latency; and TPOT — time per output token or per-token tail latency, which matters for longer generative responses. we'll measure both p95/p99 and also look at mean for baseline.

[00:48] Marta (Igneous): yeah for product we care mostly about TTFT for interactive features, target is sub 200ms p95 ideally; for longer batch generation we care about tokens/s and TPOT. one question, what's a realistic p99 for TTFT?

[01:12] Priya (SE): good q. in our experience p99 TTFT is typically ~2x p95 depending on network and cold-cache effects. for a warm KV cache on instance-optimized models we often see p95=120-180ms and p99=250-400ms on A100/GPUs, but depends on prompt length and model. we'll need to emulate their prompt distribution.

[01:38] Jon (Infra): our infra has bursty traffic, 100 RPS baseline with spikes to 350 for short windows, concurrency per user ~4. sequence lengths vary — median 80 tokens, 95th 420 tokens, and occasional 1024.

[02:05] Priya (SE): that's super helpful. for sizing the POC we usually run three profiles: low-latency interactive (short seq, focus TTFT), throughput-limited (many concurrent requests, measure tokens/sec and TPOT), and long-horizon (long seq to stress KV cache and memory).

[02:29] Alex (AE): and important to capture cold vs warm cache behavior, right? Marta: how long do you expect cold-cache windows?

[02:40] Marta: with multi-tenant caches and lots of prompt diversity, cold windows happen after a few minutes of inactivity per model variant. We want P99 to be robust even with some cold-state events.

[02:58] Priya: ok, measurement plan: 1) synthetic replay of 48-hour trace you provide, 2) steady-state load tests at 1x, 3x, and 5x baseline RPS, 3) cold-start runs where we recycle serving nodes to measure cold KV and model warm-up. We'll collect TTFT, per-token latency distribution, and tokens/sec.

[03:22] Samir (ML): what's the difference operationally between TTFT and start-of-stream handling — e.g., our client waits for first token then streams. Does Redwood measure from request arrival at edge or after auth and routing?

[03:37] Priya: good point — we measure at the Redwood ingress layer (time request received) and can also provide end-to-end synthetic runs from a client VM to capture network. for true product-visible TTFT we should do client-side measurements as well.

[03:55] Tina (Security): any considerations for VPC or private deployments? we'll need KMS integration and audit logs during the POC, and want to ensure no model data leaves our VPC for dedicated/private modes.

[04:08] Alex: yes we have Redwood Private options — can run the POC in a VPC with customer-managed KMS. we'll include security docs.

[04:20] Priya: on SLO numbers proposal: interactive feature target (Igneous asks): p95 TTFT = 150ms, p99 TTFT = 350ms; TPOT targets for generative outputs: p95 = 12ms/token, p99 = 28ms/token with 512-token median outputs. We recommend validating both cold and warm scenarios and specifying success criteria as: p95/p99 must meet target for 95% of 1-hour rolling windows during steady-state 1x load and for 90% of windows at 3x load.

[05:02] Marta: that sounds reasonable; we need to map those to user experience thresholds. Also curious about the token accounting — does TPOT vary with batch size or quantization?

[05:18] Priya: yes TPOT is sensitive to batch size and q8/q4 quantization profiles. part of the POC is to try recommended quant profiles; Redwood Optimize will provide suggestions. batching will improve throughput but can increase base TTFT slightly depending on batching latency SLOs.

[05:36] Jon: network overhead is a real one for us — some offices have higher RTT to Redwood regions. can we test from our region?

[05:45] Alex: absolutely, we'll run client-side probes from your staging VMs in your primary region to capture e2e TTFT.

[05:54] Samir: how about measurement windows and reporting — we need raw traces plus percentile aggregates. Do you provide p95/p99 by endpoint and model version?

[06:07] Priya: yes we can output per-route, per-model p95/p99 and full trace dumps (ndjson) for post-analysis. We'll also surface per-token breakdowns and KV cache hit/miss rates.

[06:22] Marta: timeline — we want to start the POC next week and run 2 weeks of tests while we evaluate. is that feasible?

[06:31] Alex: feasible. plan: week 1 config + baseline runs + iterate on prompt set; week 2 steady-state and scaled runs. we'll aim to have baseline bench results by 2027-01-25.

[06:44] Priya: measurement checklist: (a) define success criteria doc (you'll provide), (b) share traffic trace and sample prompts, (c) define model variant(s) to test (open models/quantized variants), (d) define network e2e vantage points, (e) run cold/warm and scaled runs, (f) produce report with p95/p99, raw traces, and latency bucket histograms.

[07:10] Marta: on success criteria — primary is interactive feature adoption: 95% of interactive requests under p95 TTFT target during steady-state. secondary is cost per 1k tokens under threshold we'll negotiate.

[07:28] Priya: we'll include cost profile estimates in the report (batching, quantization impacts). For fairness we'll run the same prompts across variants.

[07:43] Jon: network and kube autoscaling: we'll need to set up autoscaler thresholds so infra doesn't bottleneck the test. we'll coordinate with Redwood on node sizes.

[07:56] Alex: action items recap: Redwood runs baseline benchmarks and shares scripts; customer provides traces and security requirements; schedule load window. Any blockers?

[08:08] Tina: from security side we need SOC2 docs and KMS runbook. Alex: you'll share?

[08:14] Alex: yes, we'll share SOC2 summary and KMS integration doc after the call.

[08:21] Marta: can you also include a recommended set of metric dashboards and alert thresholds for production?

[08:28] Priya: yes we'll share dashboard templates and suggested alerts (high p99, token-rate drop, KV-miss spikes).

[08:37] Samir: small note — when you report TPOT please also include per-token variance and tail latencies, because median token rates hide jitter on long responses.

[08:47] Priya: agreed, we'll include histograms and tail breakdowns.

[08:54] Alex: great. i'll follow up with the benchmark plan and confirm dates. thanks everyone.

[09:00] (call ends)

Notes: transcription has a few speaker label inconsistencies in places; some technical terms spelled phonetically (e.g., "kv cash" instead of KV cache) in auto-generated parts.
